solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One Barking High Street

indicators.note: high can mean drunk, and a drunk staggers about in no fixed order

parts.note: taken as written, its six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone yelling on the main shopping street of Barking, a district of east London.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking looks like the London place name, and High Street like a single phrase; split them, and High is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter is a breed of gun dog, so it is one creature that barks.

clue.text: Source of oil in southeast unaltered

parts.note: compass abbreviation
unchanged, the same

explanation.surface: Tracing where some oil in the southeast comes from, finding nothing has changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesame seeds are pressed to make a widely used cooking oil.

clue.text: Sure it won't get muddled? It's hard to say

indicators.note: muddled means jumbled up, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: all thirteen letters, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone doubts that a statement will come out without confusion, and admits it is difficult to judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's hard to say' reads as uncertainty, but literally describes a phrase that is difficult to pronounce.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue twister is a phrase deliberately made difficult to pronounce quickly and correctly.

clue.text: One choosing e-reader?

parts.note: taken as written, as in e-reader
a lector is a reader, especially one who reads lessons in church

explanation.surface: Someone choosing which electronic book device to buy.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the split of e-reader into E plus a word for reader.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter in an election chooses between candidates, so is one choosing.

clue.text: Regret holding "escape" and "save"

indicators.note: holding means gripping something inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: to rue is to regret
the escape key on a keyboard is labelled Esc

explanation.surface: Someone regretting a computer that is stuck between the escape and save commands.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks hint at keyboard commands: Esc is the escape key's label.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescue someone is to save them from danger; both are verbs.

clue.text: Ultimately become parody, losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the word's first letter is dropped

parts.note: a send-up is a parody

explanation.surface: Something turns out in the end to be a mere parody, with its leader gone.
explanation.definitionFit: To end up as something is to finally turn out that way, eventually becoming it.

clue.text: Conservative faction getting share as payment

parts.note: standard abbreviation for Conservative
a side is a faction in a dispute
a ration is an allotted share

explanation.surface: A political party faction receiving its cut as a payoff.
explanation.definitionFit: In law and business, consideration is the payment or value given in return for something.

clue.text: Level, containing the French football team

indicators.note: containing means one word holds another within it

parts.note: even means level, flat
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A level football team featuring the French side.
explanation.definitionFit: A football side fields eleven players, so the team itself is called an eleven.

clue.text: Beginning to see, except when lacking light

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: the opening letter of see
unless means except when

explanation.surface: Starting to see, except where there is no light.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunless describes a place without sunlight, so dark and lacking light.

clue.text: Sees coins, tossed, splitting

indicators.note: tossed things land jumbled at random, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone watches coins being tossed to decide how to divide something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Splitting' must be read as a noun, the act of breaking away.
explanation.definitionFit: Secession is the formal withdrawal of a state from a union, a political breakaway.

clue.text: Impenetrable contents of hidden secret

indicators.note: the contents of something sit inside it, so the letters lie within the next words

parts.note: runs across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A hidden secret whose contents cannot be understood.
explanation.definitionFit: Dense foliage or prose is thick and hard to get through, so impenetrable.

clue.text: Figure lacking a horse

indicators.note: lacking means without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: a figure is an amount, a sum
taken as written, the letter removed

explanation.surface: Someone who looks like a rider without a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' reads as a person or shape; here it means a number.
explanation.definitionFit: A mount is the horse a rider sits on.

clue.text: Turn over decisive factor in what's fitting for head?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to overturn, as a boat does

definitions.text: decisive factor in what's fitting for head
definitions.meaning: second meaning, split in two words: the measurement that decides whether a hat will fit

explanation.surface: Reconsidering the deciding factor in choosing the right head of an organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'what's fitting for head' is a hat, and the factor deciding fit is its measurement, read as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat that capsizes turns over in the water.

clue.text: Gate allowing one to enter until rest dispersed

indicators.note: dispersed things are scattered about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A gate admits people one at a time until the rest of the crowd has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnstile is a rotating barrier that admits one person at a time, as at a stadium.

clue.text: Trendy drink I had is bland

parts.note: in means fashionable
a sip is a small drink
contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A fashionable drink I tried turned out to be tasteless.
explanation.definitionFit: Insipid means lacking flavour or interest, so bland.

clue.text: What may cover Pisces or Libra

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the plates covering a fish, Pisces being the Fish
second meaning: the zodiac sign symbolised by a balance

explanation.surface: Asking what falls under the star signs Pisces or Libra, as in a horoscope.
explanation.walkthrough: Pisces is the Fish of the zodiac, so what covers it is fish skin; Libra is the Balance.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish's body is covered in small plates, and Libra's symbol is a weighing balance; both go by this plural word.

clue.text: Goes off seat, second to last

indicators.note: second is abbreviated S, and sending it to last moves that opening letter round to the end

parts.note: a saddle is a rider's seat

explanation.surface: Someone leaves their seat just a moment before the end.
explanation.walkthrough: S is the abbreviation for second; the S at the front of the seat word moves round to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs that addle go bad, so the verb means goes off in the sense of spoiling.

clue.text: Greek character not favouring Italian wine

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
anti means against, not in favour

explanation.surface: A Greek person who does not care for Italian wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from the Tuscany region of Italy.

clue.text: French city hosting English relation

indicators.note: a host takes a guest in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera
standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A French city playing host to an English relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a family relation, the daughter of one's sibling.

clue.text: Small, tricky splinter

parts.note: standard abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
hard means difficult, tricky

explanation.surface: A tiny splinter that is awkward to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: A shard is a sharp broken fragment, like a splinter of glass.

clue.text: Some volume of books teaching religion

parts.note: lit is short for literature
RE is religious education, a school subject in Britain

explanation.surface: A volume of religious teaching texts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' suggests a book, but here it is a measure of capacity.
explanation.definitionFit: A litre is a metric unit of capacity, so it is a certain amount of volume.

clue.text: Put in shifts almost the whole of marriage

indicators.note: shifts means moves about, so the letters change places

parts.note: taken as written, letters to rearrange

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the whole is all of it

explanation.surface: Someone works shifts that take up nearly all of married life.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuptial is the adjective describing anything relating to marriage or a wedding.

clue.text: Dessert that's frozen, or best whipped

indicators.note: whipped means beaten up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A frozen pudding, or perhaps better whipped like cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorbet is a frozen sweet made from fruit juice or purée and sugar.

clue.text: Ace fellow is a looker

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards
a don is a fellow of a university college
taken as written

explanation.surface: A first-rate man is good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis was the handsome youth of Greek myth, so the name now means a strikingly attractive man.
